query: Which specific exogenous shocks (policy changes, regulatory thresholds, industry events) plausibly alter corporate purpose and can serve as natural experiments for causal identification?

response.query: Which specific exogenous shocks (policy changes, regulatory thresholds, industry events) plausibly alter corporate purpose and can serve as natural experiments for causal identification?
response.answer: Policy changes like new environmental regulations or industry-specific mandates, regulatory thresholds such as minimum wage laws, and industry events like mergers or crises can alter corporate purpose. These serve as natural experiments for causal identification.

results.content: IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA WRIT PETITION (C) NO. Annexure P1 A copy of email dated 28.07.2025 sent by the petitioner to the Respondent no. Whether there was/is litigation on the same point of law, if yes, details thereof: N/A NEW DELHI DATE: 17.09.2025 SYNOPSIS The instant writ petition in public interest is being filed under Article 32 of the Constitution of India seeking an appropriate writ, order or direction to the Respondent to make publicly available the complete data retrieved from the crashed Air India Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner, bearing registration VT-ANB, which met with a fatal accident on 12.06.2025 at Ahmedabad, and to appoint independent professionals to monitor the investigation, as the Respondent’s selective and incomplete disclosure of critical information, coupled with the premature attribution of pilot error while overlooking systemic faults, has resulted in a continuing violation of Article 21 and Article 14 of the Constitution of India.

results.title: Financial Value Transparency and Gainful Employment
results.content: The above authorities collectively empower the Secretary to promulgate regulations to (1) require institutions to report information about their programs to the Secretary; (2) require prospective students, with respect to certificate programs and graduate degree programs that do not meet certain financial value measures established by the Department, to acknowledge having viewed the information on the Department's program information website before entering into an enrollment agreement; (3) establish measures to determine the eligibility of GE programs for participation in title IV, HEA; and (4) require institutions to provide warnings to students and prospective students with respect to GE programs that may lose their title IV, HEA eligibility in the next year, and require the students to acknowledge having viewed the warning through the Department's program information website.
